1Distributions are taken through loans and withdrawals, which reduce a policy’s cash surrender value and death benefit and may cause the policy to lapse. Loans are not considered income and are tax-free. Withdrawals and surrenders are tax-free up to the cost basis, provided the policy is not a modified endowment contract (MEC). A MEC policy is one in which the life insurance limits exceed certain high levels of premium, or the cumulative premium payments exceed certain amounts specified under the Internal Revenue Code. For policies that are MECs, distributions during the life of the insured, including loans, are first treated as taxable to the extent of income in the contract, and an additional 10% federal income tax may apply for withdrawals made prior to age 59½.

Page.Copy:
The right life insurance policy lives alongside you, giving you options for death benefit protection and potential opportunities to grow as your life changes and priorities shift. 

Whether you're looking to provide protection for your loved ones, supplement your retirement income or create a tax-advantaged legacy, Lincoln can help align your goals with tailored solutions.1

See how life insurance can help:

ComponentArray.name: Life - The Protector - Tab - Gen comp -1
ComponentArray.Copy:
Protect what matters most

Meet Peter

Peter is married with three children. He's still working and plans on retiring in about 20 years. At this stage in his life, here are some questions Peter has: 

  • "Could my family pay household expenses if something happened to me?"

  • "Will taxes minimize the legacy I'd like to leave to my loved ones?"

  • "Could our family's future plans still happen — college, etc.?"

  • "Will we be able to sustain our current lifestyle after retirement?"

ComponentArray.name: Life - The Planners- Tab - Gen comp -1
ComponentArray.Copy:
Plan for future needs

Meet Dave and Joan

Dave and Joan are both still working but are getting close to retirement. They believe they have enough resources to continue their current lifestyle and want to maximize the amount they can leave to the surviving spouse and their children. At this stage in their lives, these are the questions they have:

  • "How can we build our estate and pass it to our two children with minimal taxes?"

  • "What's the best way for us to make sure the surviving spouse will be well taken care of and have control of our estate plan?"

ComponentArray.Copy:
Build a tax-advantaged portfolio

Meet Henry

Henry has maxed out his traditional retirement savings accounts but wanted to continue to build his retirement savings in a tax-smart way. At this stage in his life, here are some questions Henry has:

  • "When will I be able to afford to retire?"

  • "Is my retirement portfolio as tax-efficient as it can be?"

  • "How can I strengthen my portfolio during turbulent market conditions and changing political landscapes?"

  • "Is there an alternative option that provides tax advantages, but allows access without penalties?"

ComponentArray.name: Life - The bus owner - Gridblock 1 - Gen comp - 1
ComponentArray.Copy:
Business owners retain, reward, recruit

Meet Andrea

Andrea owns a business and has a key employee, Kyle. Andrea wants to reward Kyle beyond his compensation package as a way to retain him so he will stay with her company for the long term. As a business owner, Andrea has the following questions:

  • "Can I reward Kyle with additional compensation to keep him loyal to the company?"

  • "Are there ways to financially prepare for my own retirement while also retaining my key employees?"

  • "How can I gain a competitive advantage as a business owner?"
